{{One source|date=December 2023}}
In [[topology]], a branch of [[mathematics]], a '''collar neighbourhood''' of a [[manifold|manifold with boundary]] <math>M</math> is a [[neighbourhood]] of its boundary <math>\partial M</math> that has the same structure as <math>\partial M \times [0, 1)</math>.

Formally, if <math>M</math> is a [[differentiable manifold|differentiable manifold with boundary]], <math>U \subset M</math> is a ''collar neighbourhood'' of <math>M</math> whenever there is a [[diffeomorphism]] <math>f : \partial M \times [0, 1) \to U</math> such that for every <math>x \in \partial M</math>, <math>f (x, 0) = x</math>.<ref name ="Lee_2012">{{citation|title=Introduction to Smooth Manifolds|volume=218|series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics|first=John|last=Lee|publisher=Springer|year=2012|isbn=9781441999825|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xygVcKGPsNwC&pg=PA226}}</ref>{{rp|p. 222}}
Since <math>[0, 1)</math> is diffeomorphic to <math>[0, \infty)</math>, it is equivalent to take a diffeomorphism <math>f : \partial M \times [0, \infty) \to U</math>.<ref name ="Hirsch_1976">{{cite book |last1=Hirsch |first1=Morris W. |title=Differential topology |date=1976 |publisher=Springer-Verlag |location=New York Heidelberg Berlin |isbn=978-1-4684-9449-5}}</ref>{{rp|§6}}


Every differentiable manifold has a collar neighbourhood.<ref name ="Lee_2012" />{{rp|Th. 9.25}}<ref name ="Hirsch_1976" />{{rp|Th. 4.6.1}}
